title: Finite-support assembly of ordinary tensor-Hom evaluation on a ringed site
statement:
Let $(C,J,R)$ be a small ringed site with commutative coefficient sheaf under [def-weil-size-convention], and let $E,F$ be cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves. Suppose $E^i=0$ for $i<a$ or $b<i$, with $a,b\in\mathbf Z$, and for every integer $i$ and module sheaf $M$ the canonical map
$$\theta_{i,M}:M\otimes_R\mathcal Hom_R(E^i,R)\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_R(E^i,M),\qquad y\otimes\phi\longmapsto(x\mapsto y\phi(x))$$
is an isomorphism, using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Put $O=R[0]$ and $D=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(E,O)$ [def-pur-hom-complex]. The formula sending $y\otimes\phi\in F^p\otimes_R D^q$ to $x\mapsto y\phi(x)$ in degree $p+q$, with zero components on $E^r$ for $r\ne-q$, defines a chain map
$$\epsilon:\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R D)\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(E,F)$$
with the tensor differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and no additional sign. In degree $n$, the canonical finite-support identifications of its source and target with the respective sums
$$\bigoplus_{i=a}^b F^{n+i}\otimes_R(E^i)^\vee,\qquad \bigoplus_{i=a}^b\mathcal Hom_R(E^i,F^{n+i})$$
take $\epsilon^n$ to $\bigoplus_{i=a}^b\theta_{i,F^{n+i}}$. In homogeneous degrees $p,q$ the differential comparison is
$$d_Fy\otimes\phi+(-1)^{p+q+1}y\otimes(\phi d_E)\ \longmapsto\ d_Ff-(-1)^{p+q}f d_E.$$
Every $\epsilon^n$ is an isomorphism, and the degreewise inverses form an inverse chain map. No bound on $F$, K-flatness hypothesis, or finite-free retract assumption on $E$ is required.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, last three displays and final sentence; finite-support sum/product reindexing and compatibility with the Hom and tensor differentials from section-hom-complexes (original item step 5).

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-ringed-site-bounded-dual-components] for the given bounded $E$, with exactly the same small ringed site and commutative $R$. Its projection isomorphisms identify $D^q$ with $(E^{-q})^\vee$, identify its differential with $\phi\mapsto(-1)^{q+1}\phi d_E^{-q-1}$, and give $D^q=0$ outside $[-b,-a]$. Only these clauses are used; the bidual clause is unnecessary. Write $S=\{i\in\mathbf Z:a\leq i\leq b\}$, a finite set, and $T=\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R D)$, $H=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(E,F)$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, ordinary dual terms in the second paragraph; Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, Hom differential.

proof.text: By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], $T^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}F^p\otimes_R D^q$. A tensor factor with $D^q=0$ is zero: its presheaf tensor product is sectionwise zero by bilinearity, and its sheafification is zero by the universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $q$ in $[-b,-a]$ put $i=-q$; then $p=n+i$. Define an isomorphism $T^n\to A_n:=\bigoplus_{i\in S}F^{n+i}\otimes_R(E^i)^\vee$ on each surviving summand by this reindexing and step 1's projection, and on each zero summand by zero. Define its inverse on the $i$th summand by the inverse projection and the total-complex inclusion at $(n+i,-i)$. Both composites are identities after precomposition with every coproduct inclusion. Thus these are inverse sheaf maps. This argument includes $S=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, displayed terms of the tensor complex; explicit finite-support reindexing.

proof.text: By [def-pur-hom-complex], $H^n=\prod_{r\in\mathbf Z}\mathcal Hom_R(E^r,F^{r+n})$. Outside $S$ each factor is zero: on every slice there is just one linear map from the zero module sheaf, by [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Projection onto the $S$-factors and insertion of zero maps in all other factors are mutually inverse, checked on product projections. For $B_i=\mathcal Hom_R(E^i,F^{n+i})$, the finite product $P_n=\prod_{i\in S}B_i$ is also their coproduct: let $u_i:B_i\to P_n$ have $i$th component the identity and other components zero. For maps $g_i:B_i\to Z$, their extension is $\sum_{i\in S}g_i\pi_i$, since $\pi_j u_i$ is the identity for $i=j$ and zero otherwise, and $\sum_i u_i\pi_i=1$ after every product projection. Sums of morphisms are available in the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. This gives the asserted canonical identification $H^n\cong\bigoplus_{i\in S}B_i$, including the empty product, which is the zero sheaf.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, displayed terms of the Hom complex; Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, product definition.

proof.text: Construct $\epsilon^n$ before asserting its invertibility. For $p+q=n$, a section $y\in F^p(U)$ and $\phi\in D^q(U)$ determine a family with just the $r=-q$ component nonzero. On an object $V\to U$ of the slice this component sends $x\in E^{-q}(V)$ to $y|_V\,\phi_V(x)\in F^p(V)$, where $\phi$ is projected as in step 1. This is linear in $x$, compatible with restriction to every $V\to U$, additive and $R(U)$-balanced in $y,\phi$. The descriptions in [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-pur-hom-complex] therefore give a linear map from the presheaf tensor to $H^n$. The tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] extend it uniquely to $F^p\otimes_R D^q\to H^n$. The coproduct property defining $T^n$ then gives $\epsilon^n$. Its prescribed homogeneous formula contains no extra sign.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, final displayed canonical comparison; Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, homogeneous-map description.

proof.text: Check $d_H\epsilon^n=\epsilon^{n+1}d_T$ on each tensor summand and then on pure tensors before sheafification; equality there implies equality of sheaf maps by the uniqueness in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For $y$ of degree $p$ and $\phi$ of degree $q$, step 1 and [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] give $d_T(y\otimes\phi)=d_Fy\otimes\phi+(-1)^{p+q+1}y\otimes(\phi d_E)$. Put $f=\epsilon^n(y\otimes\phi)$, supported at $r=-q$. By [def-pur-hom-complex], $(d_Hf)^r=d_F^{r+n}f^r-(-1)^n f^{r+1}d_E^r$. The only possible terms are $x\mapsto(d_Fy)\phi(x)$ at $r=-q$ and $x\mapsto(-1)^{p+q+1}y\phi(d_Ex)$ at $r=-q-1$. Linearity of $d_F$ justifies the first equality on every slice. These are exactly the images of the two tensor differential terms above, and every other component is zero. Hence the maps $\epsilon^n$ form the required chain map, with precisely the differential comparison in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, differential d(f)=d_F f-(-1)^n f d_E; Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, termwise comparison.

proof.text: Under the identifications of steps 2 and 3, the $i$th source inclusion is the tensor summand at $(p,q)=(n+i,-i)$, with $D^{-i}$ identified with $(E^i)^\vee$. By step 4 its composite with the $j$th target projection is zero if $j\ne i$, and if $j=i$ it is exactly $y\otimes\phi\mapsto(x\mapsto y\phi(x))$, namely $\theta_{i,F^{n+i}}$. Coproduct inclusions and product projections determine a morphism uniquely. Consequently the matrix of $\epsilon^n$ is the finite diagonal map $\bigoplus_{i\in S}\theta_{i,F^{n+i}}$, with the stated canonical identifications, rather than an unspecified isomorphism between the two objects.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, last three displays and reduction to module evaluation.

proof.text: For each $i\in S$ the hypothesis applies to the module sheaf $M=F^{n+i}$, so $\theta_{i,F^{n+i}}$ has an inverse sheaf morphism. Form the opposite diagonal map using these inverses. Multiplying the two finite matrices gives the identity on each diagonal and zero off the diagonal, in both orders. Conjugating by steps 2 and 3 gives $g^n:H^n\to T^n$ with $g^n\epsilon^n=1$ and $\epsilon^n g^n=1$. For empty $S$ these are the unique maps between zero sheaves. Thus every actual component $\epsilon^n$ is invertible; the argument requires no bound on any degree of $F$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, final reduction to invertible module comparisons; explicit inverse matrix.

proof.text: From step 5, $d_H^n\epsilon^n=\epsilon^{n+1}d_T^n$. Composing on the left with $g^{n+1}$ and on the right with $g^n$ gives $g^{n+1}d_H^n=d_T^n g^n$. Hence the $g^n$ form an inverse chain map, and the two composites with $\epsilon$ are identities componentwise by step 7. All constructions use the bounded support of $E$, the stated termwise comparisons, and the ordinary Hom and tensor definitions. In particular no K-flat resolution, finite-free retract, or boundedness of $F$ was invoked.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, invertibility of evaluation, completed by inversion of the chain-map identity.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, last three displays and final sentence; Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes. Explicit finite-support maps, inverse matrices, and differential calculation fill in the ordinary-complex argument.
